Meshu Mokitimi (b. 1926) devoted his life to working from his studio in Maseru, creating art that documents the culture and people of Lesotho across more than seven decades. A seated figure wearing a traditional conical Basotho hat — still, weighted, entirely present.

His artistic journey began at twelve, herding cattle and making detailed clay figurines that astonished his village. He later studied design at Achimota College in Ghana, encountering African sculpture, European masters, and the philosophy of Négritude — all of which shaped his own distinctive idiom of African Expressionist art.

His remarkable life took him across the world: invited to the São Paulo Biennial in 1975; staying with Miles Davis during a 1980 American museum tour; his work collected by Bill Clinton and hanging in embassies and government buildings across Europe and America. In 2006, King Letsie III appointed him Commander of the Most Loyal Order of Ramats’eatsana for his outstanding contribution to Basotho culture.

Acquired at auction benefiting The African Library Project — a nonprofit that has established over 4,000 libraries and placed more than one million books across sub-Saharan Africa. Meshu’s biography, A Life Lived in Love, was presented to King Letsie III at a celebration in his honor in 2016.
